title: Video visual novel game
author: Kompicek
selftext: I was working on a game from 11/25 to 03/2026. It was supposed to be a visual novel with a lot of branching and a large number of endings, story focused on one character and real life mostly, but unlike normal Ren'Py slideshow games, it's built around video sequences. I abandoned it for now, even though I've got over 5 hours of gameplay. Opinions: should I continue, does it have potential, should I at least release it as a free demo? Do you think it had potential? All the videos you see are from custom-trained local models.

comments.author: Bookoora
comments.body:
We've done branching stories before. Similar to gamebooks and choose-your-path adventure games, the premise is the same - how does selecting a path or choice you make affect the actors onscreen relative to you. Making it personalized (eg. you have statistics that change based on different pathing choices) and have different endings (based on the same backend) will make it replayable and interesting. 

Of course, the actors have to show growth (not a static "choose this and the actor does that" simplicity), have causality (if i make the actor do this, will he/she regret, learn a lesson, lose something precious), etc.  
  
The concept is similar to the Korean FMV game Five Hearts under One Roof (but that's with 5 different girls with 5 different personalities), so if you do choose to go ahead, you need to up the ante - one, because it's an AI game (so expectations need to be higher), and two, there are already existing similar genres around.

Good luck. :)
